chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rib'i ibn Abdullah from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man dies, his sword, his mus'haf (Quran codex), his seal, and his coat of mail belong to his eldest son."
ai.seo_question: What personal items does the eldest son inherit from his father according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific inheritance of personal effects (*al-afrad*) by the eldest son, a ruling often discussed in contrast to the general distribution of the estate. It reflects the pre-modern context where these items held significant symbolic and practical value, with the sword and seal representing authority and the Quran signifying religious stewardship. Shia jurists utilize this narration to distinguish between specific bequests and the residual inheritance, emphasizing the continuity of the father's legacy through the primary heir.
